{{Third-party|date=January 2026}}
{{Short description|Canadian physicist and professor}}

'''Robert Mann''' is a physicist and University Professor (adjunct faculty) in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Waterloo.<ref name="UWProfile">{{cite web |title=Robert Mann |website=Physics and Astronomy, University of Waterloo |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/physics-astronomy/profile/rbmann |access-date=2026-01-14}}</ref> In April 2022, he was named a University Professor by the University of Waterloo.<ref name="UWUnivProf">{{cite web |title=Physicist Robert Mann named University Professor |website=Science, University of Waterloo |date=2022-04-04 |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/science/news/physicist-robert-mann-named-university-professor |access-date=2026-01-14}}</ref> He served as president of the Canadian Association of Physicists (CAP) in 2009–2010.<ref name="UWProfile" /><ref name="CAPNews15993">{{cite web |title=Dr. Robert Mann, University of Waterloo, appointed Editor-in-Chief for Canadian Journal of Physics |website=Canadian Association of Physicists |date=2020-09-14 |url=https://cap.ca/publications/cap-news/15993/ |access-date=2026-01-14}}</ref>

== Education ==
According to the University of Waterloo, Mann received a BSc in physics from McMaster University in 1978, and an MSc (1979) and PhD (1982) in physics from the [[University of Toronto]].<ref name="UWProfile" /> The Canadian Association of Physicists has described him as having been a postdoctoral fellow at Harvard University.<ref name="CAPNews15993" />

== Career ==
Mann was chair of the University of Waterloo Department of Physics and Astronomy from 2001 to 2008.<ref name="CAPNews15993" /> He is affiliated with the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics and the Institute for Quantum Computing.<ref name="UWProfile" /><ref name="CAPNews15993" />

In September 2020, CAP announced Mann's appointment as editor-in-chief of the ''Canadian Journal of Physics''.<ref name="CAPNews15993" /> (CAP later noted that, as of August 2024, he had been appointed Executive Editor-in-Chief of Canadian Science Publishing.)<ref name="CAPNews15993" />

== Research ==
Mann's research focuses on gravitation and quantum physics, including work related to black holes and quantum information.<ref name="UWProfile" /><ref name="CAPNews15993" /> The University of Waterloo has described his work as including contributions to black hole thermodynamics (including the area sometimes called "black hole chemistry") and to relativistic quantum information.<ref name="UWUnivProf" />

== Honours and awards ==
On April 4, 2022, the University of Waterloo named Mann a University Professor, a designation given to a maximum of two faculty members each year.<ref name="UWUnivProf" /> Awards listed by the University of Waterloo include a Distinguished Teaching Award (2010) and an Award for Excellence in Graduate Supervision (2014).<ref name="UWProfile" /> CAP has also described him as the recipient of the 2019 CAP Medal of Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching.<ref name="CAPNews15993" /> In 2026, Mann was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert Mann and Travis Craddock elected to Royal Society of Canada |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/science/news/robert-mann-and-travis-craddock-elected-royal-society-canada |website=University of Waterloo |date=2026-09-09}}</ref>
